what_this_is: Evidence captured from a real run of the built UI. Nothing here is mocked.

defect_1.what: The policy could select a message carrying no visible text -- an assistant turn whose only block is `thinking`. It was charged against the retention budget and replayed as an empty assistant message, so it was reported as kept while delivering nothing.
defect_1.fix: Skip candidates whose messageVisibleText() is empty. MessageText.ts no longer counts `thinking` blocks as visible text, so scoring and replayability agree.
tests: tests/context/hippo-retention.spec.ts :: pickRetained never keeps a candidate with no visible content

defect_2.what: The rendered v2 chat pane folds the compaction boundary into a synthetic process row and drops the boundary from detailMessages, so the boundary's retention summary was lost before any component could draw it. The v1 pane rendered it; v2 never did.
defect_2.fix: createSyntheticProcessSummary copies compactRetention onto the synthetic summary; ProcessTrace gained an optional `badge` slot; MessageRowV2 renders the pill, and renders nothing when the policy kept zero messages.
tests: ui/src/components/chat-v2/processGrouping.test.ts :: carries the retention summary off the folded boundary onto the process row
ui/src/components/chat-v2/processGrouping.test.ts :: reports no retention summary when the boundary carried none

live_proof.method: Playwright (headless chromium) drives the real server. A fresh chat receives large tool-style payloads until auto-compaction fires.
live_proof.pill_title_prefix: Selective retention (ebbinghaus-pagerank) preserved these messages word-for-word instead of folding them into the summary.

raw_boundary_record.note: Verbatim boundary event emitted by the engine during the recorded session.

honest_limits: The recording is a scripted Playwright session, not a human typing by hand.
Compaction was made to fire early by lowering agent.maxContextTokens for the recording; the value was restored afterwards.
The retention policy itself (ebbinghaus-pagerank) is the project's existing policy, unchanged by this work.
